issues.claim: All stated divisor norms generate the invariant tensor group for arbitrary F and finite B.
issues.counterevidence: Actual use has nB=0 and mu_ne in F; this forces stabilizer characters to be nth powers.
issues.impact: Unrestricted lemma false; required special case independently verified and no main-theorem failure demonstrated.
issues.repair_verification: Complete invariant-lift and divisor-orbit proof in report.

focused_acceptance.reason: Lemma 4.1 on PDF page 12 explicitly quantifies over arbitrary F and finite H-module B. For F=R, H=C2 acting on t by -t and B=Z/2, the origin has stabilizer H and the proposed norm is [t], which is not invariant because [-1] is not a square. The actual use has nB=0 and primitive ne-th roots in F; stabilizer characters then have n-th roots in F, so their tensor classes vanish and invariant lifts exist. The free divisor quotient justifies tensor exactness and the orbit-lift argument. This is a false general statement with a verified sufficient restriction already satisfied in the core application, hence Minor.

issues.counterexample: p=3, rank-one summands, [[1,0],[3,1]] mod9 lies in E but sends e1 to (1,3).
issues.counterevidence: Upper-left block with projection is a group homomorphism: off-diagonal products are divisible by p^2. Complete extension diagram and pointwise application verified.
issues.impact: Literal map description wrong; dimensional reduction remains justified by verified block calculation.
issues.repair_verification: Arbitrary finite ranks proved in report.

focused_acceptance.reason: The preimage of the embedded group modulo p does not preserve the chosen summand over Z/p^2: [[1,0],[3,1]] modulo 9 is an explicit obstruction. Nonetheless the upper-left block defines the needed homomorphism since both off-diagonal blocks are divisible by p and their product is zero modulo p^2. It yields the asserted extension map in arbitrary ranks. The failure is the restriction-of-action description, not the corrected extension mechanism; Minor is retained.

focused_acceptance.reason: The exact-sequence target in (2.3), PDF page 6, must be H^2(K,A), not H^2(L,A); L=C, K=R and A=Z/2 gives a direct distinction. This is a segment, not a short exact sequence. On PDF page 19, conjugation t^{-1}ut gives the inverse weight tau_31, not tau_13; the downstream invariant calculation uses the correct inverse. The cross-reference on page 11 is also local. These explicit corrections do not establish failure of the main non-lifting conclusions; the grouped issue remains Minor.
